Per rules: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. So verdict = same-entity. Best value: the register's canonical form? For applicant same-entity, the best value should presumably be the register's canonical form since it's the more complete/canonical "Dover Fueling Solutions UK Limited". The document is the legal instrument, but the doc's value appears to be a degraded/informal form. Hmm — the rule says for different-entity, best_value = document's. For same-entity spelling drift, the fused record should carry the canonical form — the register's. The document's "Dover Fuel Solution UK LTD" is likely OCR/extraction of the actual certificate which may genuinely say "Dover Fueling Solutions UK Ltd" but the extraction dropped "ing" and "s". Either way, same-entity, best value register's canonical form.

Verdict: same-entity, best_value: "Dover Fueling Solutions UK Limited".

Why: "Fueling Solutions vs Fuel Solution and Limited vs LTD are spelling/legal-suffix drift, not a different company."
